# 18.1 KAIYUANSHE China Open Source Annual Report: notes on the Data chapters (2023, 2024, 2025)

Sources: the English "Data" chapters of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 reports (`cosr2023/data.md`, `cosr2024/data.md`, `cosr2025/data.md`), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. All three were read in full.
Companion file: `18.1-data-claims.tsv` (469 rows). Every quote in it was machine-checked as a verbatim substring of its source file, after normalising whitespace, bold markers and table pipes.

Evidence level (METHODOLOGY §4): **C**. These are industry/self-reported analytics from KAIYUANSHE and X-lab, built on OpenDigger. Cite them as "reported by KAIYUANSHE/X-lab (OpenDigger)". Never treat them as primary fact. Wherever a figure below is "derived", we computed it from the report's tables; the report does not state it.

---

## (a) Key findings for EU–China cooperation

1. **EU vs China developer counts (2024 report, §7.1.2, Table 7.1).** On GitHub, the "European Union" has **17,281,528** active developers in 2024 (+22.68%). China has **9,404,966** (+6.11%, "the lowest among all major countries"). The table ranks the EU **2nd** and China **4th**. Of the three reports, this is the only table that treats the EU as one unit. It also lists Germany separately (3.32M), so Germany is double-counted. The basis of these figures is unexplained: they are in the millions, while the same chapter's sample has only 2.55M geolocated developers.
2. **Germany vs China on influence (2025 report, §2.2.3, Table 2-4).** On 2025 OpenRank Influence, Germany ranks **2nd (625,814)**, just ahead of China, **3rd (611,892)**. The US is 1st (1,789,364). On Contribution Impact (Table 2-3), China is 2nd (254,963) and Germany 3rd (79,742). Taken together, the EU members in the top 10 (DE, FR, NL, PL) exceed China on influence (derived: about 1.9x) but trail it on contribution impact (derived: about 0.67x).
3. **How internationalised China-led and US-led projects are (2025, §2.2.5, Table 2-5).**
   - China-led projects get **79.14%** of their contributions from China.
   - European contributors to China-led projects are Germany 1.35%, Czechia 0.73%, Sweden 0.59%, Bulgaria 0.56% and the UK 0.53%. EU members total about 3.2% (derived), well behind the US at 6.27%.
   - US-led projects get only 38.21% of contributions from the US. China supplies 7.81%, Germany 6.84%, the UK 5.92%, France 3.66%, the Netherlands 2.26% and Poland 1.86%.
   - Europeans contribute substantially to US projects but barely to Chinese ones. That gap is a measurable cooperation baseline.
4. **"One-way integration" framing (2025, §2.2.4–2.2.5).** The report itself says overseas participation in Chinese projects is "very limited". It calls this a "center-periphery" structure and says China is a "receiver". In its words, China must move from "internal circulation" to "global co-governance". This is an explicit policy signal in favour of foreign (including European) participation.
5. **High-impact developers (2025, §2.4, Table 2-6).** Counting developers with OpenRank ≥200: **Germany 159 > China 110**, UK 79, France 53, US 398. China grew 10x since 2016 (11 → 110) and Germany grew 178%. The report calls Germany, the UK, France (and Canada!) a "European Big Four".
6. **Regions (2025, §3.1, Tables 2-7 and 2-8).**
   - In the global top 15 regions, Berlin is 7th, Île-de-France 9th and Bavaria 14th. Beijing is 12th and Shanghai 15th. England is 2nd (UK).
   - In the global top-100 regions, Germany has **10 entries**, China 8 and the US 23. EU-27 members together have about 25 entries (derived).
   - The report credits Europe with "a leading role in open source governance, joint standard-setting and green computing".
7. **Projects (2025, §3.3.1, Tables 2-13 and 2-14).** OpenHarmony is #1 among global projects (60,089.18) and openEuler is #10. European-origin projects in the top 15 are **NixOS (Netherlands, #3)** and **Odoo (Belgium, #11)**. Of the 78 attributable projects in the global top 100: US 49, China 12, Germany 3, Netherlands 3, France 1 and Bulgaria 1 (EU-27 = 8, derived).
8. **Foundations (2024, §2.5).** OpenAtom ranks #1 among foundations in 2024; Apache was #1 in 2023, with OpenAtom #2. Stichting NixOS (NL) is #4 and the Godot Foundation #7, which the report presents as "European participation". This ranking depends on counting the Linux Foundation without its sub-foundations (2024 §4.1 note).
9. **Enterprises.**
   - No EU-headquartered firm appears in any global enterprise top-15 table.
   - Huawei is #2 globally in 2024 and 2025 (89,368.78 in 2025) and Alibaba #10 in 2025.
   - Hugging Face is labelled "US". Elastic and Nabu Casa/Home Assistant, which have European roots, are also listed as US (2025 Table 2-11, our annotation).
10. **Chinese AI models on Hugging Face (2025, §4.1.3h).** Citing HF's own Spring 2026 review, the report says Chinese models were **41% of HF downloads** in the past year and that China overtook the US. Qwen has more than 113,000 derivatives, and Alibaba has more derivatives than Google and Meta combined. The one EU entry in the like-resident table is FLUX.1-dev (Black Forest Labs, Germany; our annotation); 5 of the 10 are Chinese.
11. **Shift away from GitHub (2025, §2.1.3, §2.2.3).**
   - China had only about 15,000 newly active GitHub developers in 2025, against more than 1M on Gitee/AtomGit/GitCode.
   - Part of the 2025 fall in global OpenRank is blamed on "Chinese developers [shifting] from GitHub to domestic platforms".
   - This matters for any GitHub-only EU–China comparison, because China's activity on GitHub is increasingly undercounted.
12. **Licences (2023, §1.4).**
    - The report says EUPL 1.2 and EPL 2.0 drove the growth in licence types in 2017–18, and that the Mulan and CERN v2 licences emerged in 2021–22.
    - Only 220 active GitHub repos used Mulan licences by Dec 2023.
    - The 2024 licence section exists only as a hidden HTML comment in Chinese. It gives MIT ~43%, Apache-2.0 rising from 15.7% to 19.4%, and 47 licence types.
    - On Hugging Face derivatives (2025, §4.1.3f), the licence is "Unknown" for 58% of adapter edges and 68% of merge edges. That is a concrete interoperability and compliance topic for EU–China cooperation (AI Act and licence clarity).
13. **Asia–Europe working-hour overlap (2024, §6.3.5).** Activity on open-source database projects peaks at 2–6 UTC (Asia) and 6–10 UTC (Europe). The report concludes there is a "critical role of collaboration between Asia and Europe in the open-source database domain". This is an inference from time zones, not from location data.
14. **Germany as a model (2024, §1.3.2).** Germany ranks 5th by developer count but **2nd by activity** (1,492,317.89, above China's 1,097,116.82). The report recommends that China "learn from the experiences of countries with high participation like Germany".
15. **Flink as a cross-border case (2024 §4.3; 2025 §3.1.4).** Apache Flink is counted among "Chinese projects" and credited to Hangzhou/Alibaba. Its origin is German (TU Berlin/Stratosphere, later Ververica, which Alibaba acquired; our annotation). It is a ready-made EU–China case, but the classification should be flagged.

## (b) Methodology by year

| | 2023 report | 2024 report | 2025 report |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platforms | GitHub, Gitee, GitLink | GitHub, Gitee (GitLink dropped) | GitHub, Gitee, AtomGit/GitCode, GitLab, plus Hugging Face and ModelScope (new) |
| Data infrastructure | OpenDigger / X-lab; 2023 is the first year Gitee enters OpenRank (§8.1) | OpenDigger / X-lab | OpenDigger; raw data and code claimed open-sourced; OpenRank listed by MIIT ([2025] No. 19) |
| Time window | Calendar 2023 (implicit); trend charts 2019–2023 | Calendar 2024; **Oct–Dec 2024 repo metadata missing**, so 2024 language data is model-predicted (§1.4.2) | Explicitly 1 Jan–31 Dec 2025; HF monthly analysis Mar 2025–Feb 2026; trends 2016–2025 |
| Indicators | OpenRank (influence) and Activity (weighted Issue/PR/Review) | Same; OpenRank means "influence" for projects and "contribution" for developers | Restructured under OSDGs: Activity (5 behaviours: OI, ID, OPR, PRR, MPR; stars/forks excluded), community OpenRank (contribution quality), global OpenRank (PageRank-like influence), new **OpenRank Contribution Impact**; high-impact developer = OpenRank ≥200 |
| GitHub vs Gitee comparison | Top 30,000 active repos per platform, 8 event types | Same | Full-platform counts, plus "deduplication based on survey section data" (method unexplained) |
| What "China" means | Developers: self-declared GitHub location (~2M geolocated of 10M active, a "2%" sample). Projects, firms and developers: **OpenDigger labels**. Firm OpenRank = sum of projects the firm initiated, incl. those donated to foundations. Provinces include **Taiwan and Hong Kong** | Same location method (2.55M geolocated of 12M, ~120M registered); provincial tables include Taiwan and Hong Kong | OpenDigger labels covering **34 provincial-level regions "including Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan"**; country attribution of projects is by initiating organisation (78/100 attributable); enterprise ranking double-weights community and global OpenRank |
| Developer count meaning | "Active developers" 21.93M (annual, GitHub) | 25.11M annual active; separate country table in millions (EU 17.28M, China 9.40M) | 24.93M **cumulative over the decade** on GitHub; China 2.1M on GitHub, >3.5M including domestic platforms |

Recurring caveats:
- Location data is self-declared on GitHub, and China appears under-represented.
- Chinese entities are identified through OpenDigger labels that X-lab curates.
- Many rankings exist only as images: the 2023 and 2024 OpenRank top lists, the 2024 tech-domain top 10s, and the 2025 contribution Sankey. These are marked "figure-only" in the TSV.

## (c) Contradictions and series breaks

**Chinese developer totals cannot be compared across years.**
- 2023: ">20 million" across GitHub+Gitee, or 18.8M per GitHub Q3 2023, or ~12M per platform.
- 2024: 9,404,966 (and 8,863,326 for 2023).
- 2025: >2.1M on GitHub and >3.5M including domestic platforms.
- The definitions (registered, annual-active, decade-cumulative-active, extrapolated) all differ.

**China's rank among countries.**
- 2023: Table 1.1 puts China 3rd (171,039 devs, 126,238 active), but Table 7.1 in the same report puts China 2nd with 113,893 active.
- 2024: 3rd in the location sample and 4th in Table 7.1 (behind the EU).
- 2025: 3rd on GitHub; "2nd" if domestic platforms are included.

**2024 province table.** The percentages are copied unchanged from 2023 (22.04%, 16.43%, …) even though the counts changed. Its "total number" values equal the "active 2024" values in Table 7.2. Provincial growth of 45–98% does not fit national growth of 6.11%.

**GitHub totals.**
- Events: 1.4bn (2023) vs 1.75bn (2024) "≈+10%". That is actually +25%.
- Active repos: 87.92M active in 2023 vs 34.88M decade-cumulative in 2025.
- Within 2025, active repos are given as >36M and as 34.88M, GitHub additions as 5.9M and 6.32M, and GitLab as ~730k and ~700k.
- New GitHub developers in 2024: "~3.11M" (2024 report) vs 2,802,137 (2025 Table 2-1).

**Gitee vs GitHub.** The 2023 report says the events of Gitee's top-30k repos exceeded GitHub's from 2021, and that its activity did so from 2022. The 2024 report says GitHub events are "still much higher than Gitee" on the same top-30k basis. The most frequent GitHub event type changes from Push (2023) to Watch (2024).

**Enterprise ranks.**
- Alibaba: 6th globally (2023), 8th (2024), 10th (2025).
- Ant Group: "entered top ten in 2023" (2023 report) vs "entering top 15 for the first time in 2023, now 13th" (2024 report).
- Baidu: 12th globally (2024 §3.1) vs "fell 9 places to 19th" (2024 §3.4).
- Huawei: 2nd globally in 2023 (2023 and 2024 reports) vs "3rd in 2023" and also "2nd since 2022" (both in 2025 §3.2). Huawei's push is dated to 2019 in the 2023 report and to 2018 in the 2024 report.
- DaoCloud: 2024 OpenRank 6,759.34, but the 2025 change of −8,306.29 implies about 12,864.
- 2025 claims "StarRocks Inc. formerly SelectDB". This is a factual error: SelectDB is the Apache Doris company.

**Foundations.** Apache was #1 and OpenAtom #2 in 2023; OpenAtom is #1 in 2024. The 2024 note excludes Linux Foundation sub-foundations, which affects the comparison.

**OpenHarmony.** OpenRank was 67,538.71 in 2024 and 60,089.18 in 2025, a fall of about 11% that the text does not mention. openEuler was 16,728 in 2023 and 16,257.57 in 2025.

**Licences.**
- 2023: MIT is "60%" of licensed repos, yet only 1.58M of the 7.7M licensed repos (~20%) are MIT.
- 2024 hidden draft: MIT ~43%, MIT repos falling to <1M (likely an artefact of the missing Q4 data), and 47 licence types vs 46 in 2023.

**Project types.** The 2024 shares (31.4/24.3/23.2/18.9/2.3%) are effectively identical to 2023's, which suggests the data was reused. The 2024 quadrant text refers to "2023".

**2025 internal inconsistencies.**
- China–US contribution impact: the text says ~50%, but the table gives 85.6%. The text also says China's impact is "keeps rising", while the table shows −1.89%.
- The labels of Tables 2-3 and 2-4 are swapped.
- US high-impact developers grew +60%, which the text calls "doubled".
- Beijing's OpenRank appears as 1,248.72 (global table), 12,487.72 (China table), and 111,961.74 and 11,961.74 (city table and text).
- "Developers (10k)" for regions is implausible: California 5.94M is more than the US total of 5.08M, and Beijing 3.32M is more than China's total of 2.11M.
- AtomGit growth from 50k to 250k is stated as +335%; it is actually +400%.
- Hugging Face model totals are given as 2.34M, 2.5M, ~2.64M (from 1.802M = 68.3% unlabelled) and ~3.04M (from 267,328 = 8.8%).
- OSPP completion is 77% in the text but 81% in the table.
- verl is overall rank 7 in Table 2-16 but rank 12 in Table 2-15.
- The 2025 OSPP analysis excludes AtomGit, despite the platform claim in §1.2.4.

**OSPP universities.** 498 participating in 2024 (2024 report) vs 165 (−21) in 2025, which implies 186 in 2024. The definitions differ.

**Series breaks.**
- 2023 is the first year Gitee enters OpenRank, and the first year with country/foundation rankings.
- 2024 drops GitLink, adds commercial OSS and OSPP chapters, and is missing Q4 metadata.
- 2025 adopts the OSDGs framework, new indicators (Contribution Impact, a narrower activity definition), new platforms (AtomGit, GitLab, Hugging Face, ModelScope) and decade-cumulative counts.
- The 2023 developer total (21.93M annual) and the 2025 total (24.93M cumulative) are **not** the same series.

## (d) Everything about Europe/EU

These rows are flagged `about_europe = yes` in the TSV (71 rows).

**2023 report**
- §1.3.2 Table 1.1 (developers with GitHub location): DE 88,767 (#5), UK 83,245 (#6), FR 57,480 (#8), RU 47,213, PL 31,469 (#11), NL 30,617 (#13), ES 28,928 (#14). The text says "European countries … collectively ranking second in volume".
- §7.1 Table 7.1: active developers DE 64,836, UK 55,175, FR 40,341, RU 31,534. "Europe" is named as a concentration area.
- §1.4.2: the European Union Public Licence 1.2 and the CERN licence v2 are mentioned in the licence-type history.
- §2.6: country OpenRank ranking (image only).

**2024 report**
- §1.3.2: DE 126,397 (#5 by count, #2 by activity 1,492,317.89), UK 103,061 (#3 by activity), FR 78,288, RU 60,735. Germany and the UK have higher per-capita activity, and the report recommends that China learn from Germany.
- §7.1.2 Table 7.1: **European Union 17,281,528 (#2, +22.68%)**, UK 3,796,457, RU 3,404,378, DE 3,316,461 (also counted within the EU). The text says "Europe has long maintained a leading position in open-source technology and collaboration".
- §2.5: Stichting NixOS (NL) is #4 and Godot Foundation #7 among foundations: "demonstrating European participation".
- §6.3.5: Asia–Europe working-hour overlap on DB projects.
- §5.2: ClickHouse and YDB are described as Russian (Yandex).
- Hidden §1.4: EUPL 1.2.

**2025 report**
- §2.1.3 Table 2-2: DE 1.16M (#5), UK 1.02M, FR 0.72M, RU 0.62M, PL 0.41M (#10) active GitHub developers. Europe is "broadly stable" at 10–20k new developers per year per country.
- §2.2.3 Tables 2-3 and 2-4: DE #3 on contribution impact and **#2 on influence (above China)**. FR, NL, PL and CH are in the top 10. European declines are "synchronized".
- §2.2.4–2.2.5: US developers contribute to projects in DE, UK and FR. European shares of contributions to China-led projects (DE 1.35%, CZ 0.73%, SE 0.59%, BG 0.56%, UK 0.53%) and to US-led projects (DE 6.84%, UK 5.92%, FR 3.66%, NL 2.26%, PL 1.86%, CH 1.91%).
- §2.2.6: the share of Germany is rising.
- §2.4: high-impact developers DE 159, UK 79, FR 53. The "European Big Four" includes Canada. Germany is described as strong in automotive and IoT and as an "industrial software hub".
- §3.1: regions Berlin #7, Île-de-France #9, Bavaria #14, England #2. Top-100 entries: DE 10, ES 3, FR 3, NL 2, UK 2, RU 2, and 1 each for BE, CZ, FI, IE, IT, PT, SE, NO, CH, UA. Europe is credited with leadership in governance, standards and green computing.
- §3.2.1: Huawei's progress in domains "not led by Europe and the US".
- §3.3.1: NixOS (NL) #3 and Odoo (BE) #11. In the top-100 attribution: DE 3, NL 3, and 1 each for FR, BG, UK, NO, CH and IS. OpenHarmony and openEuler "changed the previous situation in which European and American projects monopolized the top positions".
- §4.1.4 (our annotation): FLUX.1-dev (Black Forest Labs, DE) tops the like-resident models.
- There is **no mention of EU policy** in any of the three Data chapters: no Cyber Resilience Act, AI Act, OSPOs, EU funding or Horizon. There is no EU–China institutional cooperation either. "Europe" appears only as a statistical comparator.

## Our annotations

Our annotations are recorded in the `method_note` column. Examples are European origins of companies or projects, and derived sums or ratios. None of them appear in the report text, and each is labelled "annotation" or "derived" in the TSV.
